Each is already an accepted DAG theorem with exactly the frozen type this parent needs, so all three are reused verbatim. The runtime allows reuse of an accepted checkpoint by Lean name when the frozen type is byte-identical (runtime.py _existing_lean_name_problem; _solve_children maps the name to the existing node; _install_parent_supplied_child_handoff returns early for accepted checkpoints). No new Lean names are reserved.
(1) Steps 1–4 are dpf_exists_orthonormal_frame_det_gram. The supplied proof itself names it as the optional child for steps 1–4.
(2) Step 5 is dgoj_covector_eq_det_mul_of_mem_span: α(b) = det(⟨τ_i, b_j⟩)·α(τ) for b in the span of an orthonormal τ. It is used with τ := σ and b := v.
(3) Step 7 is rsdic_unitOrientation_eq_or_eq_neg. The supplied proof names it as the optional child for (iv).

How the children give the parent by the supplied proof (step 6 plus arithmetic stays in the parent):
- From (1) get σ orthonormal with span σ = V := span v. Put d := det(⟨σ_i, v_j⟩). Then det G = d², d ≠ 0 and |d| ≤ ∏‖v_a‖.
- (i) det G = d² > 0.
- (ii) J = √(d²) = |d| ≤ ∏‖v_a‖ (Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs).
- (iii) Let ε := if 0 < d then 1 else −1 and ξ := ε • ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ σ, a genuine element of MultiVector P n with ξ α = ε·α(σ). IsUnitOrientationOf ξ V is witnessed by τ := σ, with the left or right disjunct according to the sign of d. Each v_j lies in span v = span σ, so (2) gives α(v) = d·α(σ) = |d|·ε·α(σ) = J·ξ(α).
- (iv) Apply (3) with v := ξ, w := ζ, Q := V. It gives ζ = ξ ∨ ζ = −ξ.
- n = 0 is covered by the general statements.

subproblems.title: Gram–Schmidt frame of an independent family: det G = (det A)², det A ≠ 0, Hadamard bound (supplied steps 1–4; Simon 6.3.4–3.5)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let v = (v_0, …, v_{n−1}) (indexed by Fin n) be a linearly independent family in ℝ^P (Euclid P). Then there is an orthonormal family σ = (σ_0, …, σ_{n−1}) in ℝ^P with span{σ_0, …, σ_{n−1}} = span{v_0, …, v_{n−1}} such that, for the n×n real matrix A with entries A_{ab} := ⟨σ_a, v_b⟩: (i) det(⟨v_a, v_b⟩)_{a,b} = (det A)²; (ii) det A ≠ 0; (iii) |det A| ≤ ∏_a |v_a|. Here ⟨·,·⟩ and |·| are the Euclidean inner product and norm.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (v : Fin n → Euclid P), LinearIndependent ℝ v → ∃ σ : Fin n → Euclid P, Orthonormal ℝ σ ∧ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range σ) = Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range v) ∧ Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (v i) (v j)) = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (σ i) (v j)) ^ 2 ∧ Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (σ i) (v j)) ≠ 0 ∧ |Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (σ i) (v j))| ≤ ∏ i, ‖v i‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–4 of the parent proof (Gram–Schmidt frame of the span, coordinates, Gram identity, Hadamard bound), i.e. Simon Ch. 6, 3.4–3.5 for one linearly independent family. This is the accepted theorem dpf_exists_orthonormal_frame_det_gram, reused with its identical frozen type.

Notation. V := span{v_0, …, v_{n−1}} ⊆ ℝ^P. G := (⟨v_a, v_b⟩)_{a,b}. For the σ constructed in step 1, A_{ab} := ⟨σ_a, v_b⟩ for a, b ∈ Fin n (Lean: Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (σ i) (v j)). Fin n carries its usual order.

1. (Orthonormal frame.)
   - Let u := gramSchmidt ℝ v be the Gram–Schmidt family of v. Let σ := gramSchmidtNormed ℝ v, so σ_a = |u_a|⁻¹·u_a.
   - Because v is linearly independent, σ is orthonormal (gramSchmidtNormed_orthonormal).
   - For every b, span{u_0, …, u_b} = span{v_0, …, v_b} (span_gramSchmidt_Iic).
   - Since v is linearly independent, every u_a ≠ 0 (gramSchmidt_ne_zero). So σ_a is a nonzero multiple of u_a, and span{σ_0, …, σ_b} = span{u_0, …, u_b} = span{v_0, …, v_b} for every b.
   - Over all indices, span(range σ) = span(range u) = span(range v) = V (span_gramSchmidtNormed_range, span_gramSchmidt).
   This proves the first two conjuncts: σ is orthonormal and span(range σ) = span(range v).
2. (Coordinates.) σ is orthonormal and spans V, so it is an orthonormal basis of V.
   - Fix b. Since v_b ∈ V, v_b = Σ_c x_c σ_c for some reals x_c. Taking the inner product with σ_a and using ⟨σ_a, σ_c⟩ = δ_{ac} gives x_a = ⟨σ_a, v_b⟩ = A_{ab}. Hence v_b = Σ_a A_{ab} σ_a.
   - A is upper triangular. If a > b, then v_b ∈ span{v_0, …, v_b} = span{σ_0, …, σ_b} by step 1. Also σ_a ⟂ σ_c for every c ≤ b < a by orthonormality. So A_{ab} = ⟨σ_a, v_b⟩ = 0.
3. ((i): Gram identity.) For all a, b, step 2 and orthonormality give
   ⟨v_a, v_b⟩ = ⟨Σ_c A_{ca}σ_c, Σ_d A_{db}σ_d⟩ = Σ_{c,d} A_{ca}A_{db}⟨σ_c, σ_d⟩ = Σ_c A_{ca}A_{cb} = (AᵀA)_{ab}.
   So G = AᵀA, and det G = det(Aᵀ)·det(A) = (det A)².
4. ((ii): det A ≠ 0.) Let x ∈ ℝ^n with Ax = 0, i.e. Σ_b A_{ab}x_b = 0 for every a. By step 2,
   Σ_b x_b v_b = Σ_b x_b Σ_a A_{ab}σ_a = Σ_a (Σ_b A_{ab}x_b)σ_a = 0.
   So x = 0 by linear independence of v. The square matrix A has trivial kernel, hence is invertible, and det A ≠ 0.
5. ((iii): Hadamard bound.)
   - A is upper triangular (step 2), so det A = ∏_b A_{bb} (Matrix.det_of_isUpperTriangular).
   - By Cauchy–Schwarz and |σ_b| = 1, |A_{bb}| = |⟨σ_b, v_b⟩| ≤ |σ_b|·|v_b| = |v_b|.
   - All factors are nonnegative, so |det A| = ∏_b |A_{bb}| ≤ ∏_b |v_b| (Finset.abs_prod, Finset.prod_le_prod₀).
6. (n = 0.) The argument covers the empty family. σ is the empty family (vacuously orthonormal) and both spans are {0}. G and A are 0×0 matrices with determinant 1. So det G = 1 = 1², det A = 1 ≠ 0, and |1| ≤ 1 = ∏_∅. ∎
proof_key_steps: σ := gramSchmidtNormed ℝ v is orthonormal, and span{σ_0,…,σ_b} = span{v_0,…,v_b} for every b; in particular span(range σ) = span(range v).
v_b = Σ_a A_{ab}σ_a with A_{ab} = ⟨σ_a, v_b⟩, and A is upper triangular.
G = AᵀA by orthonormality, so det G = (det A)².
Ax = 0 implies Σ_b x_b v_b = 0, hence x = 0 by independence, so det A ≠ 0.
det A = ∏_b ⟨σ_b, v_b⟩, and Cauchy–Schwarz gives |det A| ≤ ∏_b |v_b|.

subproblems.title: Covector expansion in an orthonormal frame: α(b) = det(⟨τ_i, b_j⟩)·α(τ) (supplied step 5)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. Let τ = (τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) (indexed by Fin n) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P (Euclid P), and let b = (b_0, …, b_{n−1}) be a family in ℝ^P with b_j ∈ span{τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}} for every j. Then for every n-covector α of ℝ^P (α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n, a continuous alternating n-linear map ℝ^P × ⋯ × ℝ^P → ℝ), α(b_0, …, b_{n−1}) = det(𝒜)·α(τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}). Here 𝒜 is the n×n real matrix 𝒜_{ij} := ⟨τ_i, b_j⟩ (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (τ i) (b j)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ b : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → (∀ j, b j ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ)) → ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, α b = (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (τ i) (b j)).det * α τ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof: α(v) = det(A)·α(σ), because alternating n-forms on the n-dimensional span are multiples of the basis determinant. Here it is stated for an arbitrary orthonormal frame τ and an arbitrary family b in its span; the parent applies it with τ := σ and b := v. This is the accepted theorem dgoj_covector_eq_det_mul_of_mem_span, reused with its identical frozen type.

1. (Basis of L.) Let L := span{τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}} (Lean: Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ)). An orthonormal family is linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent). So τ is a basis e = (e_0, …, e_{n−1}) of L whose underlying vectors are e_i = τ_i (Module.Basis.span, Module.Basis.span_apply). In particular dim L = n.
2. (Restriction.) Let α_L be the alternating n-linear form on L given by α_L(c_0, …, c_{n−1}) := α(c_0, …, c_{n−1}) for c_i ∈ L (Lean: α.toAlternatingMap.compLinearMap L.subtype). Let b'_j be b_j regarded as an element of L, which is allowed by the hypothesis b_j ∈ L. Unfolding the definitions and using e_i = τ_i gives α(b) = α_L(b') and α(τ) = α_L(e).
3. (Alternating top forms.) L has the n-element basis e, so every alternating n-linear form on L is a scalar multiple of the basis determinant det_e. Namely α_L = α_L(e)·det_e (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det). Evaluating at b' gives α_L(b') = α_L(e)·det_e(b').
4. (Coordinate matrix.) det_e(b') = det M, where M_{ij} is the i-th e-coordinate of b'_j (Module.Basis.det_apply, Module.Basis.toMatrix_apply).
   - By Module.Basis.sum_repr, b'_j = Σ_l M_{lj}e_l. Taking underlying vectors, b_j = Σ_l M_{lj}τ_l.
   - Take the inner product with τ_i and use orthonormality (⟨τ_i, τ_l⟩ = δ_{il}; Orthonormal.inner_right_fintype). This gives ⟨τ_i, b_j⟩ = M_{ij}.
   - Hence M = 𝒜.
5. (Conclusion.) By steps 2–4, α(b) = α_L(b') = α_L(e)·det_e(b') = α(τ)·det 𝒜 = det(𝒜)·α(τ).
6. (n = 0.) For the empty families both sides are α evaluated at the empty family, and the determinant of the 0×0 matrix is 1. So the identity holds, and the argument above covers this case.
   Independent check by the Leibniz formula: by multilinearity, α(b) = Σ_{f : Fin n → Fin n} (∏_j 𝒜_{f(j) j})·α(τ∘f). Terms with non-injective f vanish by alternation, and α(τ∘π) = sign(π)·α(τ) for permutations π. The Leibniz formula then gives det(𝒜)·α(τ). ∎
proof_key_steps: τ is linearly independent, hence a basis e of L = span(range τ) with e_i = τ_i.
Restrict α to L: α(b) = α_L(b') and α(τ) = α_L(e).
Alternating n-forms on the n-dimensional L are multiples of det_e: α_L = α_L(e)·det_e.
The e-coordinates of b_j are ⟨τ_i, b_j⟩ by orthonormality, so det_e(b') = det 𝒜.

subproblems.title: Two unit orientations of the same subspace agree up to sign (supplied step 7)
subproblems.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^P (Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), and let v, w ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n: continuous linear functionals on n-covectors). Suppose v and w are both unit orientations of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf v Q and IsUnitOrientationOf w Q). That is, there are orthonormal families τ, τ' : Fin n → ℝ^P with span(range τ) = Q and span(range τ') = Q such that:
- either v(α) = α(τ) for every n-covector α, or v(α) = −α(τ) for every α;
- either w(α) = α(τ') for every α, or w(α) = −α(τ') for every α.
Then w = v or w = −v.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (v w : MultiVector P n) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), IsUnitOrientationOf v Q → IsUnitOrientationOf w Q → w = v ∨ w = -v
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the parent proof: two orthonormal bases of the same n-plane differ by an orthogonal matrix, so α(τ') = ±α(τ) with a sign independent of α. Here it is stated for an arbitrary subspace Q and two arbitrary unit orientations; the parent applies it with Q := span(range v), v := ξ and w := ζ. The parent's steps 2, 3 and 5, used there with τ' in place of v, are written out below. This is the accepted theorem rsdic_unitOrientation_eq_or_eq_neg, reused with its identical frozen type.

1. (Data.) By the definition of IsUnitOrientationOf, there are:
   - orthonormal τ, τ' : Fin n → ℝ^P with span(range τ) = Q = span(range τ');
   - signs δ, δ' ∈ {1, −1} with v(α) = δ·α(τ) and w(α) = δ'·α(τ') for every n-covector α.
2. (Coordinates.) Put O_{ab} := ⟨τ_a, τ'_b⟩ for a, b ∈ Fin n. τ is orthonormal, hence linearly independent, hence a basis of span(range τ) = Q. Each τ'_b lies in span(range τ') = Q, so τ'_b = Σ_a x_a τ_a for some reals x_a. Taking the inner product with τ_a and using orthonormality gives x_a = O_{ab}. Thus τ'_b = Σ_a O_{ab}τ_a.
3. (O is orthogonal.) For all b, c, orthonormality of τ' and then of τ give
   δ_{bc} = ⟨τ'_b, τ'_c⟩ = ⟨Σ_a O_{ab}τ_a, Σ_d O_{dc}τ_d⟩ = Σ_a O_{ab}O_{ac} = (OᵀO)_{bc}.
   So OᵀO = I and (det O)² = det(Oᵀ)·det(O) = det I = 1, i.e. det O ∈ {1, −1}.
4. (Expansion.) For every n-covector α, α(τ') = det(O)·α(τ).
   - Let α_Q be the restriction of α to Q, an alternating n-linear form on Q.
   - τ is an n-element basis e of Q, so α_Q = α_Q(e)·det_e (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det).
   - Evaluating at τ' (regarded in Q) gives α(τ') = α(τ)·det_e(τ').
   - det_e(τ') is the determinant of the matrix whose (a, b) entry is the a-th e-coordinate of τ'_b. That entry is O_{ab} by step 2 and uniqueness of coordinates, so det_e(τ') = det O.
5. (Constant sign.) Fix any α. Since δ² = 1, α(τ) = δ·v(α). By steps 1 and 4,
   w(α) = δ'·α(τ') = δ'·det(O)·α(τ) = (δ·δ'·det O)·v(α).
   The number c := δ·δ'·det(O) lies in {1, −1} (steps 1 and 3) and does not depend on α.
6. (Conclusion.)
   - If c = 1, then w(α) = v(α) for every α. Continuous linear maps that agree at every point are equal, so w = v.
   - If c = −1, then w(α) = −v(α) = (−v)(α) for every α, so w = −v.
7. (n = 0.) τ and τ' are empty and Q = {0}. O is the 0×0 matrix with det O = 1, and α(τ') = α(τ) because both are the value at the empty family. Steps 1–6 apply verbatim. ∎
proof_key_steps: Write v = δ·(α ↦ α(τ)) and w = δ'·(α ↦ α(τ')) with τ, τ' orthonormal frames spanning Q and δ, δ' ∈ {±1}.
τ'_b = Σ_a O_{ab}τ_a with O_{ab} = ⟨τ_a, τ'_b⟩; OᵀO = I, so det O = ±1.
α(τ') = det(O)·α(τ) for every α, since alternating n-forms on Q are multiples of det_τ.
w(α) = (δδ'·det O)·v(α) with a sign independent of α, so w = v or w = −v.
